To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we recorded neural correlates of perception in rats, and found them to be sparsely distributed in the frontal-parietal cortex, without being concentrated in either frontal or parietial cortex.

the majority of neurons in rat medial frontal cortex do not distinguish trials with correct perception of an auditory target tone from trials without perception, and that neurons in both medial frontal cortex and posterior cortex distinguish trials with correct target tone perception from trials without target tone perception.

the neural correlates of perception in rats are sparsely distributed among neurons in the frontal-parietal cortex, with a small but significant number of neurons in both the frontal cortex and parietal cortex that are associated with perception and a larger population of neurons in both areas that are associated with motor movements, but that the neurons associated with perception are not concentrated preferentially in either the frontal or parietial cortices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of cognitive functions in the rat.
the neurophysiology of the rat frontal-parietal cortex.
the neural basis of cognition, and more specifically with the role of the prefrontal cortex and posterior pariatel cortex in attention and memory processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frontal-parietal cortex is involved in the detection of a tone and in the discrimination between different features of the stimuli.
, while the rat's frontal and parietial cortices are involved in the detection process, their role is not limited to movement control.

the rat's frontal and parietial networks are involved in perception and in decision making, as it is in the human brain, and that they are involved in the same way as it is in humans, but that the rat's network is much more sparsely populated by perception-related neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a population of neurons in the rat that are involved in the perception of a target sound, and that these neurons are located in both the frontal cortex and the posterior parietal lobe.

we have shown that the rat's auditory cortex is involved in auditory perception, and we have shown that neurons in the rat frontal cortex and parietal cortex can be involved in the perception of auditory stimuli.
we have shown that frontal cortex and posterior cortex are not the sole regions that are responsible for perception, but that they do contribute to it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural correlates of task-relevant information are not concentrated in one brain area.

the neural correlates of perception in rats are sparse and distributed, and that frontal and posterior parietals areas contribute to auditory detection performance in similar ways, without being specialized in different aspects of the task.
we have developed a novel behavioral task and an associated neural data acquisition system that allows us to record from multiple sites in rat brain simultaneously.
